profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, tagged as PTC in Linn County, Oregon, belongs to Stayton Cooperative Telephone Company, doing business as SCTC, a member owned rural telecommunications cooperative headquartered in Stayton, Oregon, serving the Stayton, Sublimity, and broader Santiam Canyon area. The cooperative was formed on January 14, 1955, through the consolidation of eighteen small independent telephone companies with combined assets of about fifteen thousand dollars at the time, and has since expanded into cable television in 1995, long distance in 1999, and fiber based internet and business connectivity, while retaining cooperative governance in which member customers vote and can serve on the board. This facility is consistent with a telephone central office or exchange building of the kind rural cooperatives operate for their member communities, functioning as network switching infrastructure rather than a commercial colocation data center; the specific meaning of the PTC designation was not confirmed. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
This facility in Lyons, Oregon, is a telephone central office operated by Stayton Cooperative Telephone Company, a rural telecommunications cooperative formed in 1955 that serves the Santiam Canyon region. The cooperative has expanded from switching infrastructure into cable television, long distance, and fiber internet, but retains its original function as network switching equipment for member communities rather than commercial colocation. Its power capacity is not published.

The facility's role in Oregon's AI infrastructure cannot be assessed from available data. Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which only 8 publish power capacity figures totaling 156.6 megawatts, and this campus ranks ninth in the state by published capacity, yet its own megawatt figure remains unpublished. Without that figure, any estimate of rack density or accelerator hosting would rest on assumptions about rural cooperative infrastructure that may not apply.

This campus does not appear to function as a commercial AI training or inference facility. Rural telephone switching buildings typically operate at much lower power densities and serve local network traffic rather than serving cloud compute tenants, and no published information indicates this facility operates at scales relevant to AI workloads. The grid availability for this location is not published.
